author: Jasmine Lobe
description: From Bloomberg's ASKB to Candidly's mission to bring expert financial guidance to everyone, Observer's first A.I. Power Index Party celebrated the leaders putting A.I. to work, and what they say comes next.
title: What A.I.’s Most Powerful Leaders Said at Observer’s A.I. Power Index Party

author: Caleb Anderson
description: Rolex, Omega and Panerai references build in regatta-specific functions. Garmin's Quatix 8 can control a boat's autopilot and navigation systems. Some prioritize rugged utility; others lean into luxury, and complications vary widely across the group, reflecting how differently watchmakers define what belongs on a sailor's wrist.
title: 7 Watches That Take Yacht Life Seriously

author: Elisa Carollo
description: The first edition of the fair at the iconic Breuer Building, now Sotheby's headquarters, feels thoughtfully and purposefully curated despite the number of exhibitors increasing 50 percent to a total of 54. The result is a focused and reasonably paced unfolding of narratives across four floors that invites new readings of the art of the 20th Century and the society it reflected.
title: At Independent 20th Century, the Biggest Draw Is the Rediscoveries

author: Roberta Naas
description: Marking his new collaboration with watchmaker Hublot, the artist describes how a small object like a watch can carry the same philosophical weight as a monumental sculpture. For Koons, the collaboration circles back to a familiar theme in his work: how objects help us understand our own place in time.
title: Jeff Koons On Balloon Dogs, Time and Why He Changed His Mind About Luxury

author: Jordan Riefe
description: Director Nicole Garton says the fair, which connects artists directly to buyers without dealers, saw a 40 percent increase in sales at its previous Los Angeles edition: "At the emerging end of the market, people are still really interested in collecting directly from artists, and they're buying in greater frequency and at higher price points than they have been."
title: While Some Traditional Fairs Scale Back, the Other Art Fair Keeps Growing

author: Sissi Cao
description: With fares reaching five figures, Bark Air is testing how far the “fur baby” economy can stretch when commercial airlines make pet travel harder. Bark Air president Michael Novotny explains how the luxury pet airline works and what makes the business difficult.
title: Bark Air President on Fixing the Very Expensive Problem of Flying With Dogs

author: Elisa Carollo
description: Several veteran galleries skipped the fair this year, while the Present section, dedicated to galleries 12 years old or younger, expanded to 55 exhibitors and produced some of the opening day's strongest and fastest sales.
title: The Armory Show’s Strongest Argument for Relevance Comes From Its Youngest Galleries

author: Caitlin White
description: With historic hotels, a growing restaurant scene and plenty of Washington wine, Spokane makes an easy first stop before heading south to Walla Walla.
title: Spokane Is the Gateway to Walla Walla Wine Country
